For decades, the way enterprise manufa
was simple. A buyer found a brand. The brand handed them a catalog.
The catalog reached a dealer. The dealer closed the sale.
That model still works in some places. It works less well almost
everywhere else. The buyer who arrives on a manufacturer's website
today has already done much of what a dealer used to do. They've
researched alternatives, narrowed options, and looked for prices. What
they haven't done is fill out a form and wait three days for a callback.
Across this audit of 100 enterprise manufacturers, the gap between
what buyers expect online and what manufacturers actually deliver is
onsistent finding. The median Buyer Enablement Score
across the cohort is 2.25 out of 10.
The harder question is how manufacturers do more on the website
without disintermediating the channels that still close most of the
revenue. A few sites in this audit point to a working pattern. The website
does the early work. The channel still closes the deal.
We hope this report is useful to the manufacturers in our cohort and to

Pre-qualified leads close faster. A buyer who arrives
with the product configured, intent expressed, and
price acknowledged shortens the rep's discovery
cycle. The site's job is discovery; the rep's job is the
close. The cohort's median primary CTA is "Learn

fields or fewer, and those manufacturers cluster in
the top quartile of Buyer Enablement Score.
